title: Unstable test triage and PR heuristics (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick reference + personal notes for dealing with flaky or nondeterministic failures encountered during code review. Keeps my steps consistent and provides a short checklist to include in PR comments so authors can iterate faster.

Context / observation notes:
- Lately seeing a spike in 'integration::session-timeout' failures on the nightly suite (job: ci/integration/session).
- Several PRs show 1/3 failures locally but consistently fail on CI, often after warm-start cache.
- Pattern: failures correlate with longer latency e2e runs and happen only when a preceding test writes to an S3-like fixture then subsequent test reads without explicit sync.

Quick triage checklist (what I do first):
1) Re-run the failing job in CI (if possible) to confirm flaky vs deterministic. Label PR with 'ci-flaky' if subsequent run passes.
2) Try to reproduce locally with same container image used by CI: docker run --rm -e CI=true ghcr.io/redwood-inference/ci-image:stable ./scripts/run-test.sh path/to/test -r 10
3) Run the single test repeatedly: for i in {1..50}; do ./bazel test //tests/that:bad_test || break; done
4) Capture logs with increased verbosity (ENV TEST_LOG_LEVEL=debug) and note exact timing of setup/teardown and any storage sync calls.
5) If failure only after cache warm-up, add a minimal sleep/sync step in the test to verify race (not a fix, just for diagnosis).

Minimal repro ask (what to request from PR author):
- A single failing test reproducer that we can run locally (no full-suite).
- Exact command used in CI (job name, image tag, env vars).
- Any infra dependencies (mock services, fixtures, local credentials) and whether the PR introduced ordering or async changes.

Heuristics for reviewer comments (short templates I leave in PRs):
- If nondeterministic: "Observed intermittent CI failure (job: <job>). Please include a minimal repro and CI run link. If test touches shared fixtures, add explicit synchronization or isolate fixtures."
- If failure seems ordering-sensitive: "This looks like an ordering/race issue. Can you try running the test in isolation and then with -j8 to catch races? Consider replacing implicit shared state with per-test fixtures."
- If failure reproducible only under load: "Works locally but fails under CI load — add stress-run artifacts or consider increasing timeouts only after verifying root cause."

Short list of labels and when to use them (for triage):
- needs-repro: no local or CI repro captured yet.
- ci-flaky: transient CI failures (passed on re-run).
- infra: failure traced to infra (s3/mount/agent/runner).
- test-smell: test is doing too much (long, networky) and should be split.

Temporary mitigations (not fixes — use sparingly):
- Mark flaky test with @flaky(max_runs=5) — only if there's a plan to remove or fix within 2 weeks.
- Skip on specific CI job with clear TODO comment and tracking ticket (INF-XXXX).
- Add a CI-only retry wrapper around a particularly brittle integration test (documented).

Debug commands I use (notes to self):
- Compare git/shas: git log --oneline -n 10 --pretty=format:\"%h %s (%an)\"
- Run single test under valgrind/rr if suspect memory race (heavy): rr record ./bazel test //tests:that && rr replay
- Quick bisect idea (if failure introduced by PRs): git bisect start origin/main HEAD -- ./scripts/run-test.sh path/to/test

Mini checklist for author follow-up (what I expect back):
- repro steps (exact command) and a short video/gifs of failing CI if flaky-show needed
- single-test failure logs (paste or attach) and whether adding a small sleep made it go away
- acceptance criteria for the test (why it's required) and plan to either stabilize or move to a separate suite

Ideas for longer-term fixes (notes / brainstorm):
- Add deterministic test harness for the storage mock (explicit flush/await semantics).
- Add 'chaos' mode in CI nightly to catch ordering races intentionally (run tests in random order).
- Improve CI runner to expose durable artifacts per-test (so we can inspect store state at failure time).
- Instrument tests with simple state hashes on setup/teardown so diffs are obvious in logs.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is the warm-cache behavior introduced by the shard rebalancer change merged last week? (See INF-3492 linked above)
- Should we make ephemeral fixture names deterministic per-run to remove cross-test contamination? Pros/cons: deterministic names help debugging but risk masking cleanup bugs.

Todo (personal):
- [ ] Draft a short RFC for "per-test artifact retention" and PI estimate (ask SRE for storage cost).
- [ ] Add a small CI job that randomly re-orders test files to surface order dependencies (prototype in infra/ci/experiment).
- [ ] Follow up with Maya on the mock-storage flush API timeline.

Random scraps / quick notes: 
- Observed stacktrace: net/http: read on closed body when rebuilding kv-cache in MockStore::apply_change -> likely teardown ordering.
- Consider: expose TEST_SYNC_POINT env var to force deterministic flushes during CI debug runs.
- Slack snippet to paste quickly: "@ci-team saw intermittent failures in job ci/integration/session (link). Reproduces ~1/20 runs. Need repro from author or advise on runner image used."

End of scratchpad.

(keeps getting messy — come back next week and reorder priorities)
